routes.name: Nigeria Tourism Visa (F5A), e-Visa or embassy
routes.summary: Single-entry tourist visa for citizens of all countries except ECOWAS states and countries with a visa waiver deal. Apply online or at an embassy. You get 30 days in Nigeria, and it can't be extended. Group or family applications up to 10 people.

other: Not for ECOWAS citizens or countries with a visa waiver agreement with Nigeria
Passport valid 6+ months, photo, return ticket
Hotel booking or host address in Nigeria
Proof of funds: 180-day bank statement
Minors need a birth certificate and parental consent letter

steps: Apply on the NIS e-Visa portal or at a Nigerian embassy
Upload documents and pay the fee
Get your e-Visa approval letter and carry a printout to Nigeria

stay.note: Single entry within the 90-day visa validity. Not extendable.

routes.name: ECOWAS free movement
routes.summary: ECOWAS citizens move and settle in member states under the bloc's free movement protocols. NIS also runs the ECOWAS biometric ID card service.

other: Stay lengths and conditions weren't on the pages I opened, so check the protocol

routes.name: Employment Visa, expatriate (R2A, STR) then CERPAC
routes.summary: For foreigners hired under a Nigerian employer's approved expatriate quota. The employer gets quota approval from the Ministry of Interior, you apply for the STR visa at a Nigerian embassy, then you regularize into a 2-year renewable permit. You can only work for the sponsoring employer.

other: Confirmed work contract with a Nigerian employer that holds a valid expatriate quota
Passport valid 6+ months, CV, degrees and transcripts, employer's application accepting immigration responsibility
Board resolution for senior managers
NIS says e-CERPAC for R2A and R3A is processed before you enter, so no post-arrival regularization

stay.note: STR visa is valid 90 days from issuance and can't be extended. Then a 2-year renewable permit.

steps: Employer applies for expatriate quota at the Ministry of Interior
Apply for the STR visa at a Nigerian embassy with all documents
Enter Nigeria and get the CERPAC (or e-CERPAC)

routes.name: CERPAC (residence permit and aliens card)
routes.summary: The residence permit and ID card for foreigners staying in Nigeria a year or more. It covers employees, business owners, students, dependants, retirees, spouses of citizens, investors and highly skilled immigrants. Apply online and give biometrics at an NIS office.

other: Apply online with passport, Nigerian visa, and proof of job, business or study
Biometrics at an NIS office
Spouses of Nigerian citizens pay nothing

routes.name: Permanent Residence Visa (N1A to N6D)
routes.summary: Permanent visa classes are N1A (spouse of a citizen), N2A/N2B (Nigerian-born who renounced), N3A to N3E (investors), N4A (highly skilled), N5A/N5B (retirees) and N6A to N6D (dependants). Some give indefinite residence, others are multi-year and renewable. Details for each are in the records below.

other: Passport valid 6+ months and police clearance from where you live
Proof of financial capacity for investor and retirement classes
Dependants of investors, retirees and N4A holders apply under N6A to N6D, and can't work on those

routes.name: N2A visa (Nigerian-born who renounced citizenship)
routes.summary: For people born Nigerian who gave up their citizenship. Valid indefinitely, residence only, no employment.

other: Passport valid 6+ months
Renunciation certificate
Attested birth certificate
Security clearance certificate
No family or group applications

routes.name: Citizenship by naturalization (Section 27)
routes.summary: Under Section 27 of the Constitution you need at least 15 years of continuous residence, good character and proof you've integrated (language and customs). Apply to the Ministry of Interior with a residence permit, proof of livelihood, tax clearance and guarantors.

other: Minimum 15 years of continuous residence
Good character and proof of integration (language and customs)
Personal application

citizenship.note: Children born after you naturalize are citizens automatically. Children born earlier apply at 18.

sources.label: NIS FAQ on permanent visas and citizenship

routes.name: Citizenship by registration, marriage (Section 26(2A))
routes.summary: Foreign spouses of Nigerian citizens can register for citizenship. You need a marriage certificate, residence permit, proof of livelihood and a guarantor.

other: Years of marriage or residence not stated on the page I opened
Special cases like a deceased husband need extra documents

routes.name: Citizenship by registration, descent (Section 26(2B))
routes.summary: Open to people with a Nigerian parent, grandparent or great-grandparent. You show proof of that ancestor's citizenship along with your own documents.

other: Proof a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent is a Nigerian citizen

citizenship.note: Up to great-grandparent per the Ministry checklist.

routes.name: Citizenship by investment
routes.summary: Requires a minimum investment of USD 1,000,000 with proof, an oath of allegiance, an MoU, police reports for the last five years and evidence of a previous visit to Nigeria.

other: Basic knowledge of Nigerian history
Must show economic self-sufficiency and meet residence requirements (years not stated)
Must not hold acquired dual citizenship or come from a country that bars dual citizenship with Nigeria

routes.name: Business Visa, single entry (F4A)
routes.summary: Single-entry visa for meetings, conferences, training, contract talks, trade fairs and job interviews. No employment. 30 days in Nigeria, not extendable.

other: Invitation letter and CAC certificate from the Nigerian host company
Passport valid 6+ months, photo, return ticket
Hotel booking or host address in Nigeria

stay.note: Single entry within the 90-day visa validity.

steps: Get an invitation letter from the Nigerian host
Apply on the NIS e-Visa portal
Upload documents and pay the fee

routes.name: Transit Visa (F3B)
routes.summary: For travelers passing through Nigeria for up to 7 days with an onward ticket. Apply on the e-Visa portal. No work, transit only.

other: Onward ticket and visa to final destination where needed
Proof of funds: 30-day bank statement
Hotel booking or host address if staying overnight
Passport valid 6+ months

routes.name: Spouse and dependants of expatriate (R2B to R2E)
routes.summary: Family members of an expatriate employed on a quota can get residence permits tied to the principal's status. Spouse, minor, adult child and aged parent (65+) categories exist.

other: Proof of relationship such as marriage or birth certificate
Copy of the expatriate's visa and a letter from the principal accepting immigration responsibility

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance, then a 2-year permit.

routes.name: Temporary Work Permit (R11, 6 months)
routes.summary: For experts invited by a company for short specialized projects like installation, maintenance, repairs or training. Needs pre-approval from the Comptroller General of Immigration. Valid 6 months, multiple entry, not renewable.

other: Visa authority letter (pre-approval) from Immigration
Return or onward ticket
Project-based or specialized tasks only

routes.name: Student Visa (R7A)
routes.summary: For international students admitted to an accredited Nigerian school. Apply online or at an embassy, then regularize into a 2-year renewable permit. Work is allowed only with approval.

other: Admission letter from an accredited Nigerian institution
Proof of minimum tuition paid
Institution's letter accepting immigration responsibility
Proof of funds (6-month statement) or sponsorship
Passport valid 6+ months

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance, then a 2-year renewable permit.

routes.name: Spouse of Nigerian Citizen Visa (N1A)
routes.summary: For spouses of Nigerian citizens. Residence only, no employment. The visa is valid 90 days to enter, then a 4-year multiple-entry residence permit.

other: Attested marriage certificate
Copy of the citizen's valid ID or passport
Evidence of stable residence in Nigeria
Police clearance certificate
Passport valid 6+ months

stay.note: Residence permit stay duration is 4 years, multiple entry.

routes.name: Investor Visa, Small scale (N3A)
routes.summary: Multiple-entry investor visa and residence permit. You must import and keep US$250,000 to US$500,000 as capital in Nigeria. Permit stay is 3 years.

investment.note: Minimum of the range, imported and retained in Nigeria

other: Must hold or have held an F4B or F4C business visa
Security clearance from place of residence
Proof of investment, business plan, certificate of incorporation or registration

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance to enter, then the residence permit.

routes.name: Investor Visa, Medium scale (N3B)
routes.summary: Multiple-entry investor visa and residence permit. You must import and keep US$500,000 to US$1,000,000 as capital in Nigeria. Permit stay is 4 years.

investment.note: Minimum of the range, imported and retained in Nigeria

other: Must hold or have held an F4B or F4C business visa
Security clearance from place of residence
Proof of investment, business plan, certificate of incorporation or registration

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance to enter, then the residence permit.

routes.name: Investor Visa, Large scale (N3C)
routes.summary: Multiple-entry investor visa and residence permit. You must import and keep US$1,000,000 to US$10,000,000 as capital in Nigeria. Permit stay is 6 years.

investment.note: Minimum of the range, imported and retained in Nigeria

other: Must hold or have held an F4B or F4C business visa
Security clearance from place of residence
Proof of investment, business plan, certificate of incorporation or registration

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance to enter, then the residence permit.

routes.name: Investor Visa, Ultra large scale (N3D)
routes.summary: Multiple-entry investor visa and residence permit. You must import and keep US$10,000,000 or more as capital in Nigeria. Permit stay is 8 years.

investment.note: Minimum of the range, imported and retained in Nigeria

other: Must hold or have held an F4B or F4C business visa
Security clearance from place of residence
Proof of investment, business plan, certificate of incorporation or registration

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance to enter, then the residence permit.

routes.name: Investor Visa, Oil, gas and power (N3E)
routes.summary: Multiple-entry investor visa and residence permit. You must import and keep US$100,000,000 or more as capital in Nigeria. Permit stay is 10 years.

investment.note: Minimum of the range, imported and retained in Nigeria

other: Must hold or have held an F4B or F4C business visa
Security clearance from place of residence
Proof of investment, business plan, certificate of incorporation or registration

stay.note: Visa valid 90 days from issuance to enter, then the residence permit.

routes.name: Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa (N4A)
routes.summary: For foreigners with skills Nigeria's economy needs. You can work and live in Nigeria for 5 years on a multiple-entry permit, and it can be extended.

other: Letter of recommendation from the Nigerian Skills Gap Assessment (under ITF)
Vetted credentials and CV or skill profile
Police report from place of residence
Passport valid, recent photo

routes.name: Retirement Visa, retiree from abroad (N5B)
routes.summary: For people 65 and older who retired abroad and want to live in Nigeria. Multiple-entry 2-year residence permit. No employment.

other: Letter of retirement and proof of retirement income
Proof of importation of funds (bank statement)
Verifiable place of residence in Nigeria
Medical insurance certificate
Security clearance from country of residence
Passport valid 6+ months

routes.name: Retirement Visa, retired in Nigeria (N5A)
routes.summary: For people 65 and older who worked in Nigeria at least 20 years and retired there. Indefinite residence.

other: At least 20 years of work in Nigeria
Evidence of previous temporary residency visa where applicable
Proof of retirement income
Medical insurance certificate
Passport valid 6+ months

routes.name: Special Immigrant Status (SIS)
routes.summary: For foreigners married to Nigerian citizens. Lets you live and work in Nigeria without an employer-tied expatriate quota. You need 5 years of residence in Nigeria and a legal marriage.

other: Legal marriage to a Nigerian citizen
5 years of residence in Nigeria
